the LTD induces a refractoriness of vesicle release machinery that is downstream of presynaptically evoked calcium entry.

the refractoriness is due to a change in the properties of the RRP, which in turn is due to a modification in the properties of a subpopulation of vesicles in the RRP, and that the refractory state of the RRP is not associated with the paired pulse plasticity.
LTD at the somatic neuromuscular synapse is a postsynaptic form of synaptic plasticity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LTD induces a presynaptic refractoriness of vesicle release machinery, which can be overcome by a high frequency stimulation.
LTD induces a presynaptic calcium-dependent form of long term depression at the amphibian NMJ.

the LTD at the neuromusclar junction is a form of synaptic plasticity that is not associated with a change in presynaptic Ca2+ entry or vesicle recycling, but is associated with a change at the level of the release ready pool of vesicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the refractoriness induced by LTD in Bufo marinus muscle is not a consequence of a change in the number of vesicles in the RRP, but is instead due to a change in the exocytosis rate of these vesicles.
the refractoriness is not due to a decrease in the number of vesicles in the RRP, but rather to a decrease in vesicle release probability.
the refractoriness is not due to depletion of the RRP of vesicles, as is the case at other synapses, but rather to a modulation of the vesicle release machinery itself.
